passages.p1: Read the following passage and mark the letter A, B, C or D on your answer sheet to indicate the best answer to each of the following questions from 1 to 10. Youth and Globalisation Globalisation has become a pervasive force shaping the trajectories of contemporary youth. Its influence extends beyond economic integration to encompass cultural exchange, education, and identity formation, compelling young people to navigate increasingly complex social landscapes. In many ways, it has redefined how young individuals perceive opportunities, relationships, and their roles within a rapidly evolving global society. One of the most noticeable impacts of globalisation is the proliferation of transnational educational and professional opportunities. Students now engage with international curricula, virtual learning environments, and cross-border collaborations, often interacting with peers and educators from diverse cultural backgrounds. [I] While such exposure enhances cognitive flexibility and employability, it simultaneously intensifies competition, necessitating continuous skill acquisition and adaptability. As a result, young people are increasingly expected to demonstrate not only academic excellence but also intercultural competence and digital literacy. Globalisation also exerts a profound influence on cultural identity. The prevalence of global media and digital platforms facilitates the diffusion of dominant cultural norms, often at the expense of indigenous traditions. [II] This dynamic engenders a tension between assimilation and preservation, leaving many young individuals grappling with fragmented or hybrid identities. Notwithstanding these challenges, globalisation enables youth to participate actively in addressing global concerns. Through digital networks, they mobilise support for issues such as climate change, social justice, and educational equality. Many young people engage in online campaigns, international forums, and collaborative initiatives aimed at fostering positive change. [III] Such engagement not only amplifies their voices but also redefines their roles as agents of change within a globalised society. In conclusion, globalisation presents a dual-edged phenomenon for modern youth. While it opens doors to unprecedented opportunities, it also introduces complexities that require careful navigation. [IV] Their capacity to critically engage with global influences will ultimately determine whether they are empowered or marginalised within this evolving landscape. Therefore, fostering adaptability, critical thinking, and cultural awareness remains essential for young people seeking to thrive in a globalised world. (Adapted from https://www.researchgate.net/publication/)

passages.p4: Read the following passage and mark the letter A, B, C or D on your answer sheet to indicate the option that best fits each of the numbered blanks from 22 to 26. Environmental Conservation Environmental conservation has never been more urgent. With over 1 million species at risk of extinction due to human activities, protecting our planet is essential. Conservation not only preserves biodiversity but also maintains vital ecosystem services like clean air, water, and fertile soil, (22) ______. A key benefit of conservation is safeguarding biodiversity. Diverse ecosystems are more resilient, better able to withstand natural disasters, and provide resources such as medicine, food, and industrial materials. By protecting natural habitats, we ensure these resources remain available for future generations. Conservation also plays a crucial role in fighting climate change. Forests, wetlands, and oceans act as carbon sinks, which absorb CO₂, regulate global temperatures, and whose effectiveness (23) ______. Economically, conservation can boost local economies through eco-tourism and sustainable resource management. In addition, due to the amount of pollution that modern devices release into the air, (24) ______. Individuals can contribute by reducing waste, recycling, and using energy-efficient appliances. Supporting conservation organizations and advocating for environmental policies are also impactful. (25) ______. In conclusion, conservation is a shared responsibility. (26) ______. When individuals, communities, and governments work together, we can protect natural resources, reduce pollution, and preserve biodiversity. Small daily actions, such as recycling, conserving water, and reducing plastic use, contribute to a healthier environment. (Adapted from https://www.conservation.org/news/)
passages.p5: Read the following passage and mark the letter A, B, C or D on your answer sheet to indicate the best answer to each of the following questions from 27 to 34. In recent decades, rapid advancements in science and technology have profoundly reshaped modern life from household management to healthcare and urban development. Scientific and technological innovations have become inextricably integrated in daily life, fundamentally transforming how individuals perform routine activities. Smart systems, powered by artificial intelligence and interconnected infrastructures, enable users to regulate domestic functions such as illumination, thermal conditions, and security with remarkable precision. By assimilating data from disparate sources, these systems generate adaptive environments that respond dynamically to users’ behavioural patterns. A prominent application can be observed in energy optimisation. Sophisticated monitoring devices allow households to analyse consumption patterns and adjust usage accordingly. Certain appliances are programmed to operate during off-peak intervals, while surplus energy derived from renewable sources may be conserved for subsequent utilisation. Consequently, overall efficiency is augmented, although the amount of money saved may fluctuate depending on consumption habits. Technological advancements have also redefined healthcare practices. Wearable devices continuously register physiological indicators, including heart rate variability and sleep quality, transmitting such data to digital platforms for comprehensive analysis. These systems are capable of detecting anomalies and issuing early alerts, thereby enabling users to undertake preventive measures before minor conditions deteriorate. Nevertheless, their efficiency remains contingent upon users’ responsiveness to the feedback provided. Furthermore, smart urban infrastructures have enhanced the administration of public systems. Real-time data collected from sensors embedded in transport networks facilitate the optimisation of traffic flow and the mitigation of congestion. While such systems cannot entirely eradicate delays, they substantially enhance efficiency and alleviate environmental impact. These developments underscore the role of technology in fostering sustainable and manageable urban environments. In conclusion, technological innovations continue to play a vital role in improving various aspects of human life. While they offer substantial benefits in efficiency, healthcare, and urban management, their limitations highlight the need for responsible and effective use to maximise their potential. (Adapted from https://dynamicscommunities.com/news/)
